briefFidelity: FAIL, and it fails as an inversion rather than a shortfall. The brief opens 'No subject at all... nothing should invite a viewer to name it.' Before I had read a word of it I named the thing six times unprompted: mandala, rose window, snowflake, bloom, flower, and for 1310661 an eclipse or an iris. 1991107 I described as a cream flower with a rotten centre and 1985692 as an ochre bloom. If a blind reviewer reaches for botanical and devotional nouns on his first pass, the no-subject requirement is not close to met. The brief then asks for 'balanced without being symmetrical'; every one of the twelve is exactly rotationally symmetric about the frame centre, six-lobed in 1243682 and 1283437, seven or eight in 1203347, annular in 1310661. It asks for 'an all-over field rather than a figure on a ground'; every token is a bright core on black, which is the definition of figure on ground, and 1203347 and 1985692 are dominated by a single central mass that occupies most of the frame. It asks for 'no single dominant element'; 1475115, 1835793 and 1203347 are one dominant element with an accompaniment. It asks for narrow tonal palette and close values so difference reads as spacing; the work runs ivory against near-black at maximum value separation with ochre as a chromatic accent, so difference reads overwhelmingly as value and hue and never as interval. Four of the five instructions are answered with their opposite. The work is accomplished and it is not this commission.
composition: There is a clear and deliberate focal hierarchy in every token and that is precisely the defect here. 1203347, 1475115 and 1835793 each centre one bright polygonal mass that dominates everything around it; 1985692 centres an ochre bloom; 1310661 centres a pale core ringed by a black annulus that functions as a halo and reinforces the figure. The frame is used only as a vignette: the subject sits dead centre, the corners are demoted to scatter, and only 1446330 and 1561509 come near an even distribution, and they get there by being mostly empty black rather than by distributing marks. Nothing anywhere is off-axis. Judged as composition in the abstract this is competent and controlled; judged against a brief demanding an all-over field with no dominant element it is the wrong picture, and 1366079 is the only tile that even approaches edge-to-edge incident.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis in the set. All twelve share the black ground, the squares-only vocabulary, the centred radial construction, the same ivory-ochre-brown-grey palette and the same outward decay into edge scatter, so 1446330 at its coldest and near-monochrome and 1985692 at its warmest and most ochre-saturated still read unmistakably as siblings. 1310661 is the formal outlier with its black annulus and 1991107 with its dark granular centre, and even those never leave the family. This is a collection and not a folder; nobody would mistake any tile for another project.
palette: The colour is clearly chosen rather than sampled: black ground, ivory, an ochre-amber accent, chocolate brown and a cool grey ramp, held identically across all twelve with no stray hue anywhere. The ground supports the drawing rather than competing with it, and the ochre does real work as the only chromatic event in 1985692 and 1733538 while 1446330 withholds it almost entirely and reads colder for it. But the brief asked for narrow, tonal, close values, and this is the opposite instrument: the ivory core of 1203347 and 1475115 sits against near-black at close to the full available value range, which is what makes the figure pop off the ground and is exactly what a close-value tonal palette would have prevented. Good palette, wrong palette.
seedVariation: Real variation, and on the axis the brief actually asked for. 1561509 and 1446330 are sparse, low-count fields of small scattered squares; 1366079 and 1985692 are dense to the edges; 1203347 is one enormous mass and 1310661 is an annulus. Core size, mark count, density and hue dominance all move independently, so these are not one work at twelve rotations. The project does not fly apart either — the shared construction holds it together, arguably too tightly. The honest weakness is convergence at the top of the density range: 1203347, 1475115 and 1835793 are the same broad pale polygon in a ring of squares and differ mainly in scale, and 1243682 and 1283437 differ mainly in how much square-in-square texture survives inside the petals.
thumbnailSurvival: Passes, and passes well. On holdout-seeds-120 the twelve still read as twelve: the huge pale mass of 1203347, the black eclipse ring of 1310661, the grey near-empty field of 1446330, the tiny star in a void of 1561509, the ochre bloom of 1985692 and the dark-centred flower of 1991107 are each identifiable at a glance and at distance. What is lost is the recursive square-in-square texture inside the petals, which becomes a warm mottle by 120, costing 1283437 and 1243682 some of their 256px distinctness, and 1203347 / 1475115 / 1835793 collapse toward one silhouette. Nothing here becomes a repeated stamp. The irony is that survival is bought by exactly the high-contrast centred figure the brief forbade.
marketResponse: Visible, consistent, and legible at 120 — but acting on the wrong quantity. I read the direction blind and without labels: stress SWELLS AND SMOOTHS the core while bleaching its internal texture, and recovery CONTRACTS it and rims it with bright white square granules, usually opening a dark centre. 1283437 recovery and 1310661 recovery are unmistakable even on holdout-states-120 because the granule rim is a value event; 1243682 gains a hard black centre dot in recovery and fattens from a sharp star to a full flower in stress. The brief asked the market to act on the DENSITY OF THE FIELD, more or fewer marks. What actually moves is the mass, silhouette and articulation of a central figure. Recovery does add mark count in granules, so it is density-adjacent at one end, but stress moves the opposite way by merging marks into a larger solid, and there is no field for density to be a property of. 1203347 is the weakest of the four: at 120 its three states differ only in the size and edge-softness of one white blob.
tokenIdentity: Holds. Across all four state triplets the token stays itself: 1310661 is recognisably the annulus in all three states, 1243682 keeps its six-lobed star through the swelling and the granulation, and 1283437 remains the same textured six-point form. Nothing is replaced by a different object under drawdown. The one place identity thins is 1203347 under stress, where the core inflates into a nearly featureless ivory mass and most of what distinguishes that seed from 1475115 or 1835793 is momentarily gone; it recovers its petal separation in the recovery frame, so it is a dip rather than a break.
artifacts: No broken rendering, and I want to be careful not to inflate these. Squares are cut by the viewBox on all four edges of essentially every tile; in the dense tokens 1985692, 1366079 and 1203347 that reads as deliberate bleed, but in the sparse ones a lone ochre or grey square hanging half off a corner — 1243682 top-left, the corner dots of 1561509, the single left-edge square repeated across most tiles — reads as leftover rather than intent. Alpha stacking muds where many squares pile up: the centre of 1366079 is an indistinct tan smear, and 1203347 stress flattens to a field with no internal information at all. No vanished strokes, no collisions that read as bugs, no empty or duplicate tile.
reasoning: This is skilled, coherent, thumbnail-robust work and it is the answer to a different brief. The decision was made in Stage 1, before I knew what had been asked: my blind description reaches for mandala, rose window, snowflake, bloom, flower, eclipse and iris, and the brief's first line is that nothing should invite a viewer to name it. That single disagreement is the whole finding, and the rest compounds it in the same direction — the brief asks for balanced but not symmetrical and every token is exactly rotationally symmetric; it asks for an all-over field with no dominant element and every token is a bright figure on a black ground with a dominant centre, at its most extreme in 1203347 and 1985692; it asks for a narrow tonal palette of close values so difference reads as spacing, and the work runs ivory against near-black with an ochre accent so difference reads as value and hue; it asks the market to act on the density of the field, and what moves is the mass and articulation of a central figure. Four of five instructions are answered with their inverse, which is not a shortfall to be graded leniently but a different artwork. briefFidelity is a gate and it fails, so the accomplishment on collectionCoherence, thumbnailSurvival and tokenIdentity cannot carry it. REFUSE.
wouldChange: Break the centre and abolish the symmetry first — remove the single rotational anchor so marks are placed across the whole frame rather than orbited around a point, which alone would end the flower reading that 1991107, 1985692 and 1243682 all trigger. Then compress the value range hard: drop the ivory core and the near-black ground toward each other so the whole set lives in a mid band the width of 1446330's greys, and cut the ochre to a tonal neighbour rather than a chromatic accent, so that what a viewer notices is the gap between two squares rather than the brightness of one. Remove the two-zone core-and-surround construction entirely, since it is what makes every tile a figure on a ground. Re-bind the market to literal mark COUNT across the whole frame — a visibly sparser or denser field, the difference between 1561509 and 1366079 as a state change rather than as a seed difference — instead of to the swelling and granulation of a central mass, which is what 1203347 and 1283437 currently show. Keep the squares-only vocabulary, the alpha overlap and the edge bleed; those are the parts that already serve interval and division.
